"""The command line, exercised as a user would type it.

Everything else in the suite calls render_svg.render() directly. This file
exists because cmd_export() sits between the command line and that call, and
a bug can live entirely in how it translates flags into arguments -- which is
exactly what happened here.
"""

import contextlib
import io
import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from drawlogic import cli, render_svg
from drawlogic.doc import new_document


def _export(argv):
  # export reports the file it wrote on stderr, which is noise in a test run.
  with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
    return cli.main(argv)


def _wired_document(title, **canvas):
  doc = new_document(title)
  doc.data["canvas"].update(canvas)
  # a drives b, and their pins face each other. (These were once the other
  # way round, which looked clean only while the router drew the wire
  # straight back through both ports.)
  doc.cells.extend([
    {"id": "a", "type": "port_in", "x": 30, "y": 30},
    {"id": "b", "type": "port_out", "x": 200, "y": 30},
  ])
  doc.nets.append({
    "id": "n1", "name": "sig", "width": 1,
    "from": {"cell": "a", "pin": "p"},
    "to": [{"cell": "b", "pin": "p", "waypoints": []}],
  })
  doc.normalize()
  return doc


class TestExportRespectsTheDocument(unittest.TestCase):
  """`export` must agree with what the document itself asks for.

  cmd_export() used to pass a concrete True/False for `arrows` and `hops` on
  every run, because `not args.no_arrows` is True whenever the flag is simply
  absent -- there is no way to tell "absent" from "explicitly wanted" once it
  has gone through `not`. render_svg.render() treats None, not True, as "defer
  to canvas.arrows" (see its docstring), so every CLI export silently forced
  both on regardless of what the file said, while the same document exported
  through the editor's /api/export correctly left them off. A document saved
  with canvas.arrows: false rendered with arrows anyway, every time.
  """

  def test_no_arrows_flag_still_forces_it_off(self):
    doc = _wired_document("arrows-on")  # canvas.arrows defaults to True
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
      src = os.path.join(tmp, "d.dlg")
      out = os.path.join(tmp, "d.svg")
      doc.save(src)
      _export(["export", src, "-o", out, "--no-arrows"])
      with open(out) as handle:
        svg = handle.read()
    self.assertNotIn("<polygon", svg,
                     "--no-arrows is an explicit override and must still work")

  def test_no_flag_and_no_override_keeps_the_default_on(self):
    doc = _wired_document("arrows-on")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
      src = os.path.join(tmp, "d.dlg")
      out = os.path.join(tmp, "d.svg")
      doc.save(src)
      _export(["export", src, "-o", out])
      with open(out) as handle:
        svg = handle.read()
    self.assertIn("<polygon", svg,
                  "a document with nothing said about arrows still defaults "
                  "to drawing them")

  def test_cli_and_direct_render_agree_for_every_combination(self):
    for arrows_flag, hops_flag in ((False, False), (False, True),
                                   (True, False), (True, True)):
      with self.subTest(canvas_arrows=arrows_flag, canvas_hops=hops_flag):
        doc = _wired_document("combo", arrows=arrows_flag, hops=hops_flag)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
          src = os.path.join(tmp, "d.dlg")
          out = os.path.join(tmp, "d.svg")
          doc.save(src)
          _export(["export", src, "-o", out])
          with open(out) as handle:
            cli_svg = handle.read()
        direct_svg = render_svg.render(doc)
        self.assertEqual(cli_svg, direct_svg,
                         "CLI export must match what the document itself "
                         "renders to, the same claim the manual makes about "
                         "editor and CLI export agreeing byte for byte")


def _shorted_document():
  """Two nets drawn by hand down one line: the drawing says they are joined."""
  doc = new_document("shorted", 600, 420)
  doc.cells.extend([
    {"id": "in1", "type": "port_in", "x": 60, "y": 100, "label": "in1"},
    {"id": "in2", "type": "port_in", "x": 60, "y": 200, "label": "in2"},
    {"id": "U1", "type": "and2", "x": 160, "y": 100},
  ])
  doc.nets.extend([
    {"id": "n1", "name": "s1", "from": {"cell": "in2", "pin": "p"},
     "to": [{"cell": "U1", "pin": "a", "waypoints": [[120, 205], [120, 110]]}]},
    {"id": "n2", "name": "s2", "from": {"cell": "in1", "pin": "p"},
     "to": [{"cell": "U1", "pin": "b", "waypoints": [[120, 105], [120, 130]]}]},
  ])
  doc.normalize()
  return doc


def _validate(doc, *flags):
  """Run `validate` over a document and hand back (exit code, output)."""
  out = io.StringIO()
  with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "d.dlg")
    doc.save(path)
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
      code = cli.main(["validate", path] + list(flags))
  return code, out.getvalue()


class TestValidateRunsTheDrcs(unittest.TestCase):
  """`validate` checks how a drawing reads, not only what it references.

  Reference faults and rule failures are two halves of one question -- is
  this drawing fit to hand to someone else -- so they come out of one command
  and one exit code rather than needing two runs to find out.
  """

  def test_a_drc_error_fails_the_command(self):
    code, output = _validate(_shorted_document())
    self.assertEqual(code, 1, "a drawing with a hidden short exited 0")
    self.assertIn("on top of each other", output)
    self.assertIn("wire-short", output,
                  "the rule that found it is the heading to look up, so the "
                  "message has to name it")

  def test_no_drc_skips_them(self):
    """The escape hatch has to actually let a drawing through, or it is not
    an escape hatch."""
    code, output = _validate(_shorted_document(), "--no-drc")
    self.assertEqual(code, 0)
    self.assertNotIn("on top of each other", output)

  def test_a_clean_drawing_still_passes(self):
    doc = _wired_document("clean")
    code, _ = _validate(doc)
    self.assertEqual(code, 0)


class TestDoctor(unittest.TestCase):
  """`doctor` answers "do the pieces of this copy still fit each other".

  Three bug reports in a row were one thing: files copied over one at a time,
  leaving the Python and the JavaScript from different versions of the project
  calling into functions the other half no longer had. Each looked like a real
  bug -- a browser that would not draw, a Check that crashed, a colour picker
  that was not there -- and none of them was visible by reading a file.
  """

  def run_doctor(self):
    out = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
      code = cli.main(["doctor"])
    return code, out.getvalue()

  def test_a_healthy_copy_passes(self):
    code, output = self.run_doctor()
    self.assertEqual(code, 0, output)
    self.assertIn("consistent with itself", output)

  def test_it_exercises_the_python_rather_than_inspecting_it(self):
    code, output = self.run_doctor()
    self.assertEqual(code, 0)
    for step in ("route a wire", "check the rules", "lay it out",
                 "render to SVG"):
      self.assertIn(step, output)

  def test_the_documented_output_is_what_it_prints(self):
    """DOCUMENTATION.md shows a sample run, and the counts in it had drifted
    to a symbol and a file behind the real thing without anything noticing."""
    code, output = self.run_doctor()
    self.assertEqual(code, 0, output)
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    with open(os.path.join(here, "..", "DOCUMENTATION.md")) as handle:
      documented = handle.read()
    counted = [line for line in output.splitlines()
               if any(char.isdigit() for char in line)
               # Version, interpreter and install path are this machine's,
               # not the project's: a folder named "user1" is not a count.
               and not line.startswith(("drawlogic ", "python ", "here "))]
    self.assertTrue(counted, output)
    for line in counted:
      # assertIn would print the whole of DOCUMENTATION.md on a failure.
      self.assertTrue(line in documented,
                      "DOCUMENTATION.md's sample doctor output lacks %r" % line)

  def test_it_notices_a_module_missing_a_function_another_calls(self):
    """The Check crash: drc asks render_svg for cell_label_box, and an older
    render_svg does not have one."""
    real = render_svg.cell_label_box
    del render_svg.cell_label_box
    try:
      code, output = self.run_doctor()
    finally:
      render_svg.cell_label_box = real
    self.assertEqual(code, 1)
    self.assertIn("cell_label_box", output)

  def test_it_notices_a_browser_import_nothing_exports(self):
    """The blank editor: tools.js imported handlePoints from a selection.js
    that had not been updated to export it."""
    from drawlogic import cli as cli_module
    problems, count = cli_module._js_imports(
      os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(cli_module.__file__)),
                   "web", "js"))
    self.assertGreater(count, 0, "found no browser modules to check")
    self.assertEqual(problems, [])

  def test_the_browser_check_can_actually_fail(self):
    """Otherwise it reports a clean bill on anything, which is the shape of
    bug it exists to catch."""
    from drawlogic import cli as cli_module
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
      with open(os.path.join(tmp, "one.js"), "w") as handle:
        handle.write('import { missing } from "./two.js";\n')
      with open(os.path.join(tmp, "two.js"), "w") as handle:
        handle.write("export function present() {}\n")
      problems, count = cli_module._js_imports(tmp)
    self.assertEqual(count, 2)
    self.assertEqual(len(problems), 1)
    self.assertIn("missing", problems[0])


if __name__ == "__main__":
  unittest.main()


class TestImport(unittest.TestCase):
  """`import` writes a drawing per module and never overwrites unasked."""

  VERILOG = ("module top (input a, output y);\n"
             "  leaf u (.a(a), .y(y));\n"
             "endmodule\n"
             "module leaf (input a, output y);\n"
             "  not g (y, a);\n"
             "endmodule\n")

  def run_import(self, argv):
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
      try:
        code = cli.main(argv)
      except SystemExit as exc:
        code = exc.code
    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

  def test_it_writes_one_drawing_per_module_and_names_the_top(self):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
      source = os.path.join(tmp, "design.v")
      with open(source, "w") as handle:
        handle.write(self.VERILOG)
      code, out, _ = self.run_import(["import", source])
      self.assertEqual(code, 0)
      self.assertEqual(sorted(f for f in os.listdir(tmp) if f.endswith(".dlg")),
                       ["leaf.dlg", "top.dlg"])
      self.assertIn("top.dlg  (top)", out)

  def test_it_refuses_to_overwrite_anything_without_force(self):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
      source = os.path.join(tmp, "design.v")
      with open(source, "w") as handle:
        handle.write(self.VERILOG)
      mine = os.path.join(tmp, "leaf.dlg")
      with open(mine, "w") as handle:
        handle.write("mine")
      code, _, _ = self.run_import(["import", source])
      self.assertIn("leaf.dlg", str(code))
      self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(os.path.join(tmp, "top.dlg")))
      with open(mine) as handle:
        self.assertEqual(handle.read(), "mine")
      code, _, _ = self.run_import(["import", source, "--force"])
      self.assertEqual(code, 0)
      self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(tmp, "top.dlg")))

  def test_bad_verilog_is_reported_with_its_line(self):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
      source = os.path.join(tmp, "bad.v")
      with open(source, "w") as handle:
        handle.write("module m (input a);\n  junk;\nendmodule\n")
      code, _, _ = self.run_import(["import", source])
      self.assertIn("bad.v: line 2: cannot read", str(code))

"""Linked components: part of a drawing defined once and placed many times.

What matters: a selection becomes a drawing of its own with a port for every
wire crossing its edge, named by the wire and never by where it sits in a
list; the selection is replaced by one instance with those wires reattached
to its pins; every instance follows its definition; one made independent
stops following it alone; and a pin that disappears from a definition is
reported, never quietly swapped for another.

Usage:

    python3 -m unittest tests.test_components
"""

import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

from drawlogic import components, server, sheets
from drawlogic.doc import Document, new_document
from drawlogic.symbols import default_registry


def chain():
  """din -> a -> b -> c -> dout, with din also feeding b, all in a container."""
  doc = new_document("chain", 900, 400)
  doc.data["containers"] = [{"id": "k", "title": "Lane", "x": 120, "y": 120,
                             "w": 300, "h": 160}]
  doc.cells.extend([
    {"id": "pi", "type": "port_in", "x": 40, "y": 195, "label": "din"},
    {"id": "a", "parentId": "k", "type": "inv", "x": 150, "y": 180},
    {"id": "b", "parentId": "k", "type": "and2", "x": 280, "y": 175},
    {"id": "c", "type": "inv", "x": 520, "y": 180},
    {"id": "po", "type": "port_out", "x": 700, "y": 195, "label": "dout"},
  ])
  doc.nets.extend([
    {"id": "n1", "name": "x", "from": {"cell": "pi", "pin": "p"},
     "to": [{"cell": "a", "pin": "a"}, {"cell": "b", "pin": "b"}]},
    {"id": "n2", "from": {"cell": "a", "pin": "y"}, "to": [{"cell": "b", "pin": "a"}]},
    {"id": "n3", "label": "q", "from": {"cell": "b", "pin": "y"},
     "to": [{"cell": "c", "pin": "a"}]},
    {"id": "n4", "from": {"cell": "c", "pin": "y"}, "to": [{"cell": "po", "pin": "p"}]},
  ])
  doc.normalize()
  return doc


def errors(doc, registry=None):
  return [str(i) for i in doc.validate(registry) if i.level == "error"]


class TestPlanning(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_one_port_per_crossing_wire_named_from_it(self):
    found = components.plan(chain(), default_registry(), {"a", "b"})
    self.assertEqual(found["problems"], [])
    self.assertEqual(found["ports"], [
      {"key": "n1", "name": "x", "dir": "in", "width": 1},
      {"key": "n3", "name": "q", "dir": "out", "width": 1}])

  def test_a_loose_end_is_explained_before_anything_changes(self):
    doc = chain()
    doc.nets[2]["to"].append({"x": 600, "y": 300})
    before = doc.dumps()
    found = components.plan(doc, default_registry(), {"a", "b"})
    self.assertEqual(len(found["problems"]), 1)
    self.assertIn("loose end", found["problems"][0])
    with self.assertRaises(components.ComponentError):
      components.extract(doc, default_registry(), {"a", "b"}, "Half")
    self.assertEqual(doc.dumps(), before)

  def test_nothing_to_make_a_component_of(self):
    self.assertTrue(components.plan(chain(), default_registry(), {"k_nope"})["problems"])


class TestExtracting(unittest.TestCase):

  def setUp(self):
    self.root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    self.doc = chain()
    self.doc.path = os.path.join(self.root, "top.dlg")
    self.child, self.ref, self.instance = components.extract(
      self.doc, default_registry(), {"k"}, "Half cell", names={"n3": "result"})
    target = sheets.child_path(self.doc.path, self.ref)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target))
    self.child.save(target)
    self.doc.save()

  def tearDown(self):
    shutil.rmtree(self.root, ignore_errors=True)

  def test_the_definition_is_a_sound_drawing_of_the_selection(self):
    child = Document.load(os.path.join(self.root, "components", "half_cell.dlg"))
    self.assertEqual(self.ref, "components/half_cell.dlg")
    self.assertEqual(errors(child), [])
    kinds = sorted((c.get("type"), c.get("label") or "") for c in child.cells)
    self.assertEqual(kinds, [("and2", ""), ("inv", ""), ("port_in", "x"),
                             ("port_out", "result")])
    # The container came along, holding what it held.
    self.assertEqual([b["id"] for b in child.containers], ["k"])
    self.assertEqual(child.cell("a")["parentId"], "k")
    self.assertNotIn("parentId", child.containers[0])
    # The wire between the two stayed inside.
    self.assertIn({"cell": "a", "pin": "y"}, [n["from"] for n in child.nets])

  def test_the_parent_holds_one_instance_wired_by_name(self):
    doc, registry, problems = sheets.open_document(os.path.join(self.root, "top.dlg"))
    self.assertEqual(problems, [])
    self.assertEqual(errors(doc, registry), [])
    self.assertEqual(sorted(c["id"] for c in doc.cells), ["c", "pi", "po", "u_half_cell"])
    self.assertEqual(self.instance, "u_half_cell")
    net = {n["id"]: n for n in doc.nets}
    self.assertEqual(net["n1"]["to"], [{"cell": "u_half_cell", "pin": "x", "waypoints": []}])
    self.assertEqual(net["n3"]["from"], {"cell": "u_half_cell", "pin": "result"})
    self.assertEqual(net["n3"]["label"], "q")
    symbol = registry.for_cell(doc.cell("u_half_cell"))
    self.assertEqual(sorted(p["name"] for p in symbol.pins), ["result", "x"])
    self.assertEqual(doc.containers, [])

  def test_port_names_go_by_wire_not_by_order(self):
    one = chain()
    two = chain()
    first = components.extract(one, default_registry(), {"a", "b"}, "H",
                               names={"n1": "IN", "n3": "OUT"})[0]
    second = components.extract(two, default_registry(), {"a", "b"}, "H",
                                names=dict(reversed(list({"n1": "IN", "n3": "OUT"}.items()))))[0]
    self.assertEqual(first.dumps(), second.dumps())
    self.assertEqual(one.dumps(), two.dumps())

  def test_two_ports_cannot_share_a_name(self):
    with self.assertRaises(components.ComponentError):
      components.extract(chain(), default_registry(), {"a", "b"}, "H",
                         names={"n1": "same", "n3": "same"})

  def test_definition_edits_reach_every_instance_and_lost_pins_are_reported(self):
    path = os.path.join(self.root, "top.dlg")
    doc = Document.load(path)
    doc.cells.append({"id": "u2", "type": "sheet", "ref": self.ref, "x": 300, "y": 300,
                      "label": "H2"})
    doc.save()
    child_path = os.path.join(self.root, "components", "half_cell.dlg")
    child = Document.load(child_path)
    # Rename the output port and add a new input.
    next(c for c in child.cells if c.get("label") == "result")["label"] = "renamed"
    child.cells.append({"id": "p_en", "type": "port_in", "x": 80, "y": 300, "label": "en"})
    child.save()
    doc, registry, _problems = sheets.open_document(path)
    for cell_id in ("u_half_cell", "u2"):
      pins = sorted(p["name"] for p in registry.for_cell(doc.cell(cell_id)).pins)
      self.assertEqual(pins, ["en", "renamed", "x"])
    # The wire that used "result" still says "result": reported, not moved.
    self.assertEqual(doc.nets[[n["id"] for n in doc.nets].index("n3")]["from"],
                     {"cell": "u_half_cell", "pin": "result"})
    self.assertTrue(any("pin 'result'" in e for e in errors(doc, registry)), errors(doc, registry))


class TestPreviews(unittest.TestCase):
  """An instance can show a miniature of what its definition holds."""

  def setUp(self):
    from tests import ROOT
    from drawlogic import render_svg
    self.render = render_svg.render
    self.doc, self.registry, problems = sheets.open_document(
      os.path.join(ROOT, "examples", "gpu_arch.dlg"))
    self.assertEqual(problems, [])
    self.colour = "#8a9ba4"

  def marks(self, svg):
    import re
    return re.findall(r'<(rect|path)[^>]*stroke="%s"' % self.colour, svg)

  def test_drawn_for_an_instance_that_asks(self):
    shown = len(self.marks(self.render(self.doc, self.registry)))
    # Eight SMs, each its five blocks and its internal wires.
    self.assertGreaterEqual(shown, 8 * 5)
    for cell in self.doc.cells:
      cell.pop("preview", None)
    self.assertEqual(self.marks(self.render(self.doc, self.registry)), [])

  def test_a_definition_edit_shows_in_the_preview(self):
    root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
      shutil.copytree(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(self.doc.path)), os.path.join(root, "ex"))
      top = os.path.join(root, "ex", "gpu_arch.dlg")
      before = len(self.marks(self.render(*sheets.open_document(top)[:2])))
      child = Document.load(os.path.join(root, "ex", "components", "sm.dlg"))
      child.cells.append({"id": "extra", "type": "block", "x": 1100, "y": 400})
      child.save()
      after = len(self.marks(self.render(*sheets.open_document(top)[:2])))
      self.assertEqual(after - before, 8)
    finally:
      shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)

  def test_the_editor_draws_the_same_preview(self):
    from tests.test_js_parity import NODE, _browser_render
    if not NODE:
      self.skipTest("node is not installed")
    import re
    svg = self.render(self.doc, self.registry)
    exported = sorted(
      [tag, d if tag == "path" else "%s,%s,%s,%s" % (x, y, w, h)]
      for tag, x, y, w, h, d in [
        (m.group(1), *(re.search(r'%s="([^"]*)"' % k, m.group(0)).group(1)
                        if re.search(r'%s="([^"]*)"' % k, m.group(0)) else None
                        for k in ("x", "y", "width", "height", "d")))
        for m in re.finditer(r'<(rect|path)[^>]*stroke="%s"[^>]*>' % self.colour, svg)])
    browser = _browser_render(self.doc, self.registry)["preview"]
    self.assertEqual(len(browser), len(exported))
    self.assertEqual(browser, exported)


class TestThroughTheEditorsServer(unittest.TestCase):

  @classmethod
  def setUpClass(cls):
    cls.root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    handler = type("BoundHandler", (server.Handler,), {
      "root": cls.root, "registry": default_registry(), "quiet": True,
    })
    cls.httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler)
    cls.base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % cls.httpd.server_port
    threading.Thread(target=cls.httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

  @classmethod
  def tearDownClass(cls):
    cls.httpd.shutdown()
    cls.httpd.server_close()
    shutil.rmtree(cls.root, ignore_errors=True)

  def post(self, route, payload):
    request = Request(self.base + route, data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
                      headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    try:
      with urlopen(request) as response:
        return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except HTTPError as caught:
      return caught.code, json.loads(caught.read().decode("utf-8") or "{}")

  def setUp(self):
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(self.root, "lanes"), ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(self.root, "lanes"))
    self.doc = chain().ordered()

  def test_plan_then_create_then_make_one_independent(self):
    status, plan = self.post("/api/component", {
      "action": "plan", "doc": self.doc, "source": "lanes/top.dlg", "ids": ["a", "b"],
      "name": "Half"})
    self.assertEqual(status, 200, plan)
    self.assertEqual((plan["path"], plan["exists"]), ("lanes/components/half.dlg", False))
    status, made = self.post("/api/component", {
      "action": "create", "doc": self.doc, "source": "lanes/top.dlg", "ids": ["a", "b"],
      "name": "Half", "names": {"n1": "x", "n3": "y"}})
    self.assertEqual(status, 200, made)
    self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, "lanes", "components", "half.dlg")))
    self.assertIn("sheet:components/half.dlg", made["sheets"])
    # Made again without asking to replace it: refused, nothing written.
    status, _ = self.post("/api/component", {
      "action": "create", "doc": self.doc, "source": "lanes/top.dlg", "ids": ["a", "b"],
      "name": "Half"})
    self.assertEqual(status, 409)

    doc = made["doc"]
    doc["cells"].append(dict(next(c for c in doc["cells"] if c["id"] == made["instance"]),
                             id="u_two", label="HALF 1", x=300, y=320))
    status, copied = self.post("/api/component", {
      "action": "copy", "doc": doc, "source": "lanes/top.dlg", "cell": "u_two"})
    self.assertEqual(status, 200, copied)
    refs = {c["id"]: c.get("ref") for c in copied["doc"]["cells"]}
    self.assertEqual(refs["u_two"], "components/half_2.dlg")
    self.assertEqual(refs[made["instance"]], "components/half.dlg")
    self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, "lanes", "components", "half_2.dlg")))

  def test_a_component_needs_a_saved_drawing(self):
    status, answer = self.post("/api/component", {
      "action": "plan", "doc": self.doc, "ids": ["a"], "name": "x"})
    self.assertEqual(status, 400)
    self.assertIn("save this drawing first", answer.get("error", ""))

  def test_resolve_reads_definitions_fresh(self):
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(self.root, "lanes", "components"), exist_ok=True)
    child = new_document("blk")
    child.cells.append({"id": "p", "type": "port_in", "x": 40, "y": 40, "label": "go"})
    child.save(os.path.join(self.root, "lanes", "components", "blk.dlg"))
    self.doc["cells"].append({"id": "u9", "type": "sheet", "ref": "components/blk.dlg",
                              "x": 500, "y": 300})
    status, answer = self.post("/api/resolve", {"doc": self.doc, "source": "lanes/top.dlg"})
    self.assertEqual(status, 200, answer)
    self.assertEqual([p["name"] for p in answer["sheets"]["sheet:components/blk.dlg"]["pins"]],
                     ["go"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
  unittest.main()

"""Containers: titled boundaries that own part of a drawing.

What matters is that ownership is the `parentId` field and nothing else: it
survives a save, the checker catches every way it can be wrong, and the box is
drawn beneath what it holds, the same in the editor as in an exported file.

Usage:

    python3 -m unittest tests.test_containers
"""

import re
import unittest

from drawlogic import containers, layout, render_svg
from drawlogic.doc import Document, new_document
from drawlogic.symbols import default_registry

from tests import EXAMPLE
from tests.test_js_parity import NODE, _browser_render


def nested():
  """A GPC holding a TPC holding two gates, a note, and a wire leaving it."""
  doc = new_document("nested", 900, 600)
  doc.data["containers"] = [
    {"id": "gpc", "title": "GPC 0", "x": 40, "y": 60, "w": 460, "h": 360},
    {"id": "tpc", "parentId": "gpc", "title": "TPC 0", "x": 60, "y": 110,
     "w": 260, "h": 140, "style": {"headerFill": "#76b900", "titleFill": "#ffffff"}},
  ]
  doc.cells.extend([
    {"id": "a", "parentId": "tpc", "type": "and2", "x": 80, "y": 170},
    {"id": "b", "parentId": "tpc", "type": "inv", "x": 200, "y": 175},
    {"id": "out", "type": "port_out", "x": 700, "y": 185},
  ])
  doc.shapes.append({"id": "note", "parentId": "gpc", "kind": "text",
                     "x": 60, "y": 400, "text": "two SMs"})
  doc.nets.extend([
    {"id": "n1", "from": {"cell": "a", "pin": "y"}, "to": [{"cell": "b", "pin": "a"}]},
    {"id": "n2", "from": {"cell": "b", "pin": "y"}, "to": [{"cell": "out", "pin": "p"}]},
  ])
  doc.normalize()
  return doc


def faults(doc):
  return [str(issue) for issue in doc.validate()
          if issue.level == "error"]


class TestTheFile(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_containment_survives_a_save(self):
    doc = nested()
    again = Document.loads(doc.dumps())
    self.assertEqual(again.cell("a")["parentId"], "tpc")
    self.assertEqual(again.shapes[0]["parentId"], "gpc")
    self.assertEqual([(b["id"], b.get("parentId")) for b in again.containers],
                     [("gpc", None), ("tpc", "gpc")])
    self.assertEqual(again.containers[1]["style"]["headerFill"], "#76b900")
    # And saving it again changes nothing: the file is canonical.
    self.assertEqual(again.dumps(), doc.dumps())

  def test_a_drawing_without_containers_saves_as_it_always_did(self):
    with open(EXAMPLE) as handle:
      text = handle.read()
    doc = Document.loads(text)
    doc.containers  # asking for them must not add an empty list to the file
    self.assertNotIn('"containers"', doc.dumps())
    self.assertEqual(doc.dumps(), text)

  def test_a_new_container_is_given_its_padding_and_header(self):
    doc = nested()
    self.assertEqual(doc.containers[0]["padding"], 20)
    self.assertEqual(doc.containers[0]["headerHeight"], 32)


class TestChecking(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_a_sound_nesting_has_no_faults(self):
    self.assertEqual(faults(nested()), [])

  def test_a_missing_parent(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.cell("a")["parentId"] = "gone"
    self.assertEqual(faults(doc),
                     ["error: cell a: parent container 'gone' does not exist"])

  def test_a_parent_that_is_not_a_container(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.cell("a")["parentId"] = "b"
    self.assertEqual(faults(doc), ["error: cell a: parent 'b' is a cell, not a container"])

  def test_a_loop(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.containers[0]["parentId"] = "tpc"
    found = faults(doc)
    self.assertEqual(len(found), 1, found)
    self.assertIn("loop", found[0])
    # And it can still be drawn, so it can still be fixed.
    self.assertEqual(len(containers.paint_order(doc)), 2)

  def test_more_than_one_parent(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.cell("a")["parentId"] = ["tpc", "gpc"]
    self.assertEqual(len(faults(doc)), 1)
    self.assertIn("must name one container", faults(doc)[0])

  def test_an_id_used_by_two_kinds_of_thing(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.containers[1]["id"] = "a"
    found = faults(doc)
    self.assertIn("error: container a: id is also used by a cell", found)


class TestGeometry(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_descendants_go_all_the_way_down(self):
    self.assertEqual(containers.descendants(nested(), {"gpc"}),
                     {"gpc", "tpc", "a", "b", "note"})

  def test_fit_holds_the_contents_with_padding_and_header(self):
    doc = nested()
    registry = default_registry()
    box = doc.containers[1]
    self.assertTrue(containers.fit(doc, registry, box))
    inner = containers.contents_box(doc, registry, box)
    self.assertEqual(box["x"], inner[0] - 20)
    self.assertEqual(box["y"], inner[1] - 20 - 32)
    self.assertEqual(box["x"] + box["w"], inner[0] + inner[2] + 20)
    self.assertEqual(box["y"] + box["h"], inner[1] + inner[3] + 20)
    self.assertFalse(containers.fit(doc, registry, {"id": "empty", "x": 0, "y": 0,
                                                    "w": 10, "h": 10}))

  def test_a_cropped_export_takes_the_container_in(self):
    doc = nested()
    box = doc.content_bbox()
    self.assertLessEqual(box[0], 40)
    self.assertLessEqual(box[1], 60)


class TestDrawing(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_beneath_everything_outer_first(self):
    svg = render_svg.render(nested())
    self.assertLess(svg.index('class="dl-containers"'), svg.index('class="dl-shapes"'))
    self.assertLess(svg.index('data-id="gpc"'), svg.index('data-id="tpc"'))
    self.assertIn('fill="#76b900"', svg)

  def test_nothing_is_written_for_a_drawing_without_any(self):
    self.assertNotIn("dl-container", render_svg.render(Document.load(EXAMPLE)))

  def test_a_title_is_escaped(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.containers[0]["title"] = "<GPC> & \"0\""
    svg = render_svg.render(doc)
    self.assertIn("&lt;GPC&gt; &amp; &quot;0&quot;", svg)
    self.assertNotIn("<GPC>", svg)

  def test_a_long_title_is_cut_short_in_a_narrow_box(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.containers[1]["title"] = "Texture processing cluster number zero"
    doc.containers[1]["w"] = 120
    titles = re.findall(r'class="dl-container-title"[^>]*>([^<]*)<', render_svg.render(doc))
    self.assertEqual(titles[0], "GPC 0")
    self.assertTrue(titles[1].endswith("\u2026"), titles[1])
    self.assertLess(len(titles[1]), 20)


def gpcs(columns=2):
  """A GPU holding four GPCs in a row, each a grid of four SMs, placed badly
  on purpose, with wires from a host into each GPC and out to an L2."""
  doc = new_document("four GPCs", 1200, 800)
  doc.data["containers"] = [{"id": "gpu", "title": "GPU", "x": 40, "y": 60,
                             "w": 300, "h": 200, "layout": {"mode": "row"}}]
  spots = [(700, 300), (90, 500), (400, 80), (900, 600)]
  for g, (gx, gy) in enumerate(spots):
    doc.data["containers"].append({
      "id": "g%d" % g, "parentId": "gpu", "title": "GPC %d" % g, "x": gx, "y": gy,
      "w": 100, "h": 100, "layout": {"mode": "grid", "columns": columns}})
    for s in range(4):
      doc.cells.append({"id": "g%d_sm%d" % (g, s), "parentId": "g%d" % g,
                        "type": "block", "x": gx + 37 * (3 - s), "y": gy + 23 * s})
  doc.cells.append({"id": "host", "type": "block6", "x": 600, "y": 700})
  doc.cells.append({"id": "l2", "type": "block8", "x": 100, "y": 100})
  for g in range(4):
    doc.nets.append({"id": "in%d" % g, "from": {"cell": "host", "pin": "out%d" % (1 + g % 3)},
                     "to": [{"cell": "g%d_sm0" % g, "pin": "in1"}]})
    doc.nets.append({"id": "out%d" % g, "from": {"cell": "g%d_sm3" % g, "pin": "out1"},
                     "to": [{"cell": "l2", "pin": "in%d" % (1 + g)}]})
  doc.normalize()
  return doc


def box_of(doc, item_id):
  for kind, items in (("cell", doc.cells), ("container", doc.containers)):
    for item in items:
      if item["id"] == item_id:
        return containers.item_box(doc, default_registry(), kind, item)
  return None


class TestLayingOut(unittest.TestCase):

  def setUp(self):
    self.doc = gpcs()
    self.result = layout.arrange(self.doc, default_registry())

  def test_four_gpcs_in_a_row(self):
    boxes = [box_of(self.doc, "g%d" % g) for g in range(4)]
    # One row, in the order they read across before: GPC 1, 2, 0, 3.
    tops = set(round(b[1], 3) for b in boxes)
    self.assertEqual(len(tops), 1, boxes)
    lefts = sorted((b[0], name) for b, name in zip(boxes, ["g0", "g1", "g2", "g3"]))
    self.assertEqual([name for _x, name in lefts], ["g1", "g2", "g0", "g3"])
    for (a, _), (b, _) in zip(lefts, lefts[1:]):
      self.assertGreaterEqual(b - a, boxes[0][2])

  def test_each_gpc_is_a_two_column_grid(self):
    for g in range(4):
      sms = [box_of(self.doc, "g%d_sm%d" % (g, s)) for s in range(4)]
      self.assertEqual(len(set(round(b[0], 3) for b in sms)), 2)
      self.assertEqual(len(set(round(b[1], 3) for b in sms)), 2)
      outer = box_of(self.doc, "g%d" % g)
      for sm in sms:
        self.assertGreaterEqual(sm[0], outer[0])
        self.assertGreaterEqual(sm[1], outer[1] + containers.header(self.doc.containers[1 + g]))
        self.assertLessEqual(sm[0] + sm[2], outer[0] + outer[2])
        self.assertLessEqual(sm[1] + sm[3], outer[1] + outer[3])

  def test_every_container_holds_its_contents(self):
    registry = default_registry()
    for box in self.doc.containers:
      inner = containers.contents_box(self.doc, registry, box)
      self.assertGreaterEqual(inner[0], box["x"])
      self.assertGreaterEqual(inner[1], box["y"] + containers.header(box))
      self.assertLessEqual(inner[0] + inner[2], box["x"] + box["w"])
      self.assertLessEqual(inner[1] + inner[3], box["y"] + box["h"])

  def test_wires_still_name_the_real_pins(self):
    self.assertEqual(self.doc.nets[0]["to"][0], {"cell": "g0_sm0", "pin": "in1",
                                                 "waypoints": []})
    names = set(c["id"] for c in self.doc.cells)
    for net in self.doc.nets:
      for end in [net["from"]] + net["to"]:
        self.assertIn(end["cell"], names)
    self.assertFalse(any(str(c.get("type", "")).startswith("__container__")
                         for c in self.doc.cells))
    self.assertEqual(faults(self.doc), [])

  def test_a_second_layout_changes_nothing(self):
    first = self.doc.dumps()
    layout.arrange(self.doc, default_registry())
    self.assertEqual(self.doc.dumps(), first)

  def test_the_result_says_what_was_done(self):
    self.assertEqual(str(self.result), "18 cells in 5 containers")


class TestLayingOutAroundPins(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_a_pinned_cell_and_its_containers_stay(self):
    doc = gpcs()
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
    doc.cell("g2_sm1")["pinned"] = True
    doc.cell("g2_sm1")["x"] += 40
    held = box_of(doc, "g2_sm1")
    gpc = box_of(doc, "g2")
    note = layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
    self.assertEqual(box_of(doc, "g2_sm1"), held)
    self.assertEqual(box_of(doc, "g2")[:2], gpc[:2])
    self.assertIn("GPC 2, GPU stayed put", str(note))
    # Nothing packed on top of the pinned SM.
    for s in (0, 2, 3):
      other = box_of(doc, "g2_sm%d" % s)
      self.assertFalse(other[0] < held[0] + held[2] and held[0] < other[0] + other[2]
                       and other[1] < held[1] + held[3] and held[1] < other[1] + other[3])


class TestLayingOutOneContainer(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_nothing_outside_it_moves(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.cell("b")["x"] += 77
    outside = (dict(doc.cell("out")), dict(doc.containers[0]))
    corner = (doc.containers[1]["x"], doc.containers[1]["y"])
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry(), container="tpc")
    self.assertEqual((doc.cell("out"), doc.containers[0]), outside)
    self.assertEqual((doc.containers[1]["x"], doc.containers[1]["y"]), corner)
    # And the note held by the GPC, outside the TPC, stayed too.
    self.assertEqual(doc.shapes[0]["y"], 400)

  def test_top_to_bottom_puts_what_drives_above_what_it_drives(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.containers[1]["layout"] = {"direction": "tb"}
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry(), container="tpc")
    a, b = box_of(doc, "a"), box_of(doc, "b")
    self.assertLess(a[1] + a[3], b[1])

  def test_notes_in_a_container_travel_with_its_contents(self):
    doc = nested()
    registry = default_registry()
    # Moved well away from where the layout will put the GPC's contents, so
    # a note left behind would show.
    containers.move(doc, {"tpc"}, 300, 200)

    def offset():
      corner = containers.contents_box(doc, registry, doc.containers[0])
      return (doc.shapes[0]["x"] - corner[0], doc.shapes[0]["y"] - corner[1])

    before = offset()
    layout.arrange(doc, registry)
    self.assertNotEqual(containers.contents_box(doc, registry, doc.containers[0])[:2],
                        (360, 310))
    self.assertEqual(tuple(round(v, 6) for v in offset()),
                     tuple(round(v, 6) for v in before))

  def test_an_unknown_layout_is_a_warning(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.containers[0]["layout"] = {"mode": "spiral"}
    warned = [str(i) for i in doc.validate() if "spiral" in i.message]
    self.assertEqual(len(warned), 1, warned)


def across_a_title():
  """A wire whose straight path runs along a container's header band, right
  through the words of its title."""
  doc = new_document("across", 1000, 400)
  doc.data["containers"] = [{"id": "mem", "title": "Memory subsystem",
                             "x": 300, "y": 100, "w": 400, "h": 200}]
  doc.cells.extend([
    {"id": "d", "type": "inv", "x": 100, "y": 101},
    {"id": "l", "type": "inv", "x": 800, "y": 101},
  ])
  doc.nets.append({"id": "n", "from": {"cell": "d", "pin": "y"},
                   "to": [{"cell": "l", "pin": "a"}]})
  doc.normalize()
  return doc


def through_band(points, band):
  """The runs of a path that touch a box: none, for a wire that keeps off."""
  hits = []
  for a, b in zip(points, points[1:]):
    x0, x1 = sorted((a[0], b[0]))
    y0, y1 = sorted((a[1], b[1]))
    if not (x1 < band[0] or x0 > band[2] or y1 < band[1] or y0 > band[3]):
      hits.append((a, b))
  return hits


class TestWiresKeepOffTitles(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_a_wire_keeps_a_clearance_off_the_whole_header_band(self):
    from drawlogic import routing
    doc = across_a_title()
    band = containers.header_box(doc.containers[0], routing.CLEARANCE - 0.5)
    [(_net, [points])] = routing.route_all(doc)
    self.assertEqual(through_band(points, band), [])
    # And it is not that the wire happened to miss: straight, it would not.
    start = points[0]
    self.assertTrue(band[1] <= start[1] <= band[3])

  @unittest.skipUnless(NODE, "node is not installed")
  def test_the_editor_routes_it_the_same_way(self):
    import os
    import tempfile
    from drawlogic import routing
    from tests.test_js_parity import _browser_result, _rounded
    doc = across_a_title()
    handle, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".dlg")
    os.close(handle)
    try:
      doc.save(path)
      browser = _browser_result(path, default_registry())
    finally:
      os.unlink(path)
      if os.path.exists(path + ".bak"):
        os.unlink(path + ".bak")
    expected = [[net["id"], _rounded(branches)]
                for net, branches in routing.route_all(doc)]
    self.assertEqual([[i, _rounded(b)] for i, b in browser["routes"]], expected)


def into_from_above():
  """A driver above a container, wired to a block inside it whose pin faces
  left. No corner or crossover reaches the pin without cutting through the
  header band, so only a path round the side gets there."""
  doc = new_document("into", 1000, 700)
  doc.data["containers"] = [{"id": "sa", "title": "System agent",
                             "x": 300, "y": 300, "w": 500, "h": 200}]
  doc.cells.extend([
    {"id": "src", "type": "block", "x": 450, "y": 120},
    {"id": "a", "parentId": "sa", "type": "block", "x": 340, "y": 370},
    {"id": "b", "parentId": "sa", "type": "block", "x": 560, "y": 370},
  ])
  doc.nets.append({"id": "n", "from": {"cell": "src", "pin": "out1"},
                   "to": [{"cell": "b", "pin": "in1"}]})
  doc.normalize()
  return doc


class TestAPathRoundTheHeader(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_a_wire_into_a_container_from_above_goes_round_the_header(self):
    from drawlogic import drc, routing
    doc = into_from_above()
    band = containers.header_box(doc.containers[0], routing.CLEARANCE - 0.5)
    [(_net, [points])] = routing.route_all(doc)
    self.assertEqual(through_band(points, band), [])
    # In through a side of the box, below the band.
    box = doc.containers[0]
    sides = [(a, b) for a, b in zip(points, points[1:]) if abs(a[1] - b[1]) < 1e-6
             and min(a[0], b[0]) < box["x"] + box["w"] < max(a[0], b[0])]
    self.assertTrue(sides, points)
    self.assertEqual([v for v in drc.check(doc) if v.level == "error"], [])

  def test_without_the_path_finder_it_would_cut_the_band(self):
    from drawlogic import routing
    doc = into_from_above()
    band = containers.header_box(doc.containers[0])
    saved = routing._find_path
    routing._find_path = lambda *args: None
    try:
      [(_net, [points])] = routing.route_all(doc)
    finally:
      routing._find_path = saved
    self.assertNotEqual(through_band(points, band), [])

  def test_a_boxed_in_end_finds_no_path(self):
    from drawlogic import routing
    sheet = routing.Sheet(boxes=[(0, 0, 100, 100)])
    self.assertIsNone(routing._find_path((50, 50), (300, 50), (1, 0), (-1, 0), sheet))

  @unittest.skipUnless(NODE, "node is not installed")
  def test_the_editor_finds_the_same_path(self):
    import os
    import tempfile
    from drawlogic import routing
    from tests.test_js_parity import _browser_result, _rounded
    doc = into_from_above()
    handle, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".dlg")
    os.close(handle)
    try:
      doc.save(path)
      browser = _browser_result(path, default_registry())
    finally:
      os.unlink(path)
      if os.path.exists(path + ".bak"):
        os.unlink(path + ".bak")
    expected = [[net["id"], _rounded(branches)]
                for net, branches in routing.route_all(doc)]
    self.assertEqual([[i, _rounded(b)] for i, b in browser["routes"]], expected)


def runs_along_outlines(doc, routes):
  """Every run lying closer than a cell's clearance to a container outline,
  alongside it -- the wire that reads as part of the box."""
  from drawlogic import routing
  found = []
  for net, branches in routes:
    for points in branches:
      for a, b in zip(points, points[1:]):
        for box in doc.containers:
          x, y, w, h = box["x"], box["y"], box["w"], box["h"]
          if abs(a[1] - b[1]) < 1e-6:
            lines = [(y, x, x + w), (y + h, x, x + w)]
            fixed, lo, hi = a[1], min(a[0], b[0]), max(a[0], b[0])
          else:
            lines = [(x, y, y + h), (x + w, y, y + h)]
            fixed, lo, hi = a[0], min(a[1], b[1]), max(a[1], b[1])
          for line, line_lo, line_hi in lines:
            if (abs(line - fixed) < routing.CLEARANCE
                and lo < line_hi and hi > line_lo):
              found.append((net["id"], a, b, box["id"]))
  return found


class TestWiresKeepOffOutlines(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_an_outline_is_crossed_but_not_followed(self):
    from drawlogic import routing
    sheet = routing.Sheet()
    sheet.add_borders([{"x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 100, "h": 100}])
    # Alongside the left edge, inside or out: not free, on any pass.
    for x in (-5, 0, 5):
      for gap in (routing.WIRE_GAP, routing.TOUCHING):
        self.assertFalse(sheet.free(False, x, 20, 80, False, gap), (x, gap))
    self.assertTrue(sheet.free(False, 15, 20, 80))
    # Straight across it is how a wire gets in, so it stays free.
    self.assertTrue(sheet.free(True, 50, -40, 40))
    # Past the end of the edge is not alongside it.
    self.assertTrue(sheet.free(False, 0, 120, 160))

  def test_four_cores_in_a_grid_wire_out_through_the_gaps(self):
    from drawlogic import routing
    from tests import ROOT, open_example
    import os
    doc, registry, _issues = open_example(os.path.join(ROOT, "examples", "cpu_arch.dlg"))
    self.assertEqual(layout_of_cores(doc), "grid")
    self.assertEqual(runs_along_outlines(doc, routing.route_all(doc, registry)), [])


def layout_of_cores(doc):
  return layout.layout_of(containers.by_id(doc)["cores"])[0]


class TestPackingLeavesRoomForWires(unittest.TestCase):

  def gaps(self, mode):
    """The gaps a packed container leaves between four blocks, each with a
    wire out to a ring beside it."""
    doc = new_document("packed", 1200, 800)
    doc.data["containers"] = [{"id": "c", "title": "Cores", "x": 0, "y": 0,
                               "w": 100, "h": 100, "layout": {"mode": mode}}]
    for i in range(4):
      doc.cells.append({"id": "b%d" % i, "parentId": "c", "type": "block",
                        "x": 200 * i, "y": 0})
    doc.cells.append({"id": "ring", "type": "block8", "x": 1000, "y": 0})
    for i in range(4):
      doc.nets.append({"id": "n%d" % i, "from": {"cell": "b%d" % i, "pin": "out1"},
                       "to": [{"cell": "ring", "pin": "in%d" % (i + 1)}]})
    doc.normalize()
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
    boxes = sorted(box_of(doc, "b%d" % i) for i in range(4))
    if mode == "row":
      return [b[0] - (a[0] + a[2]) for a, b in zip(boxes, boxes[1:])]
    return [b[1] - (a[1] + a[3]) for a, b in zip(boxes, boxes[1:])]

  def test_a_row_widens_for_the_wires_leaving_it(self):
    from drawlogic import drc
    # Four wires: a wire gap each after the first, a cell's clearance either
    # side.
    want = 2 * drc.WIRE_TO_CELL + 3 * drc.WIRE_GAP
    for gap in self.gaps("row"):
      self.assertAlmostEqual(gap, want)

  def test_a_column_keeps_the_plain_gap(self):
    from drawlogic import drc
    for gap in self.gaps("column"):
      self.assertAlmostEqual(gap, drc.CONTAINER_GAP)

  def test_blocks_with_no_wires_keep_the_plain_gap(self):
    from drawlogic import drc
    doc = gpcs()
    doc.nets[:] = []
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
    sms = sorted(box_of(doc, "g0_sm%d" % s) for s in range(4))
    self.assertAlmostEqual(sms[2][0] - (sms[0][0] + sms[0][2]), drc.CONTAINER_GAP)


def wired_column():
  """Rename above a reorder buffer above schedulers, in a column, rename
  wired to both: two wires that have to loop round the side."""
  doc = new_document("column", 1200, 800)
  doc.data["containers"] = [{"id": "oe", "title": "OoO engine", "x": 0, "y": 0,
                             "w": 100, "h": 100, "layout": {"mode": "column"}}]
  for i, name in enumerate(("ren", "rob", "sch")):
    doc.cells.append({"id": name, "parentId": "oe", "type": "block",
                      "x": 100, "y": 150 * i})
  doc.nets.append({"id": "alloc", "from": {"cell": "ren", "pin": "out1"},
                   "to": [{"cell": "rob", "pin": "in1"}]})
  doc.nets.append({"id": "disp", "from": {"cell": "ren", "pin": "out2"},
                   "to": [{"cell": "sch", "pin": "in1"}]})
  doc.normalize()
  layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
  return doc


class TestColumnLoopsGetLanes(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_the_column_stays_one_column(self):
    doc = wired_column()
    lefts = set(round(box_of(doc, c)[0], 3) for c in ("ren", "rob", "sch"))
    self.assertEqual(len(lefts), 1)

  def test_each_side_has_room_for_its_loops(self):
    from drawlogic import drc
    doc = wired_column()
    box = doc.containers[0]
    pad = containers.padding(box)
    blocks = [box_of(doc, c) for c in ("ren", "rob", "sch")]
    left = min(b[0] for b in blocks) - box["x"]
    right = box["x"] + box["w"] - max(b[0] + b[2] for b in blocks)
    # Two wires leave on the right, two loads come in on the left.
    want = 2 * drc.WIRE_TO_CELL + drc.WIRE_GAP
    self.assertGreater(want, pad)
    self.assertAlmostEqual(left, want)
    self.assertAlmostEqual(right, want)

  def test_the_two_loops_run_in_lanes_of_their_own(self):
    from drawlogic import drc, routing
    doc = wired_column()
    routes = dict((net["id"], branches) for net, branches in routing.route_all(doc))
    right = max(b[0] + b[2] for b in (box_of(doc, c) for c in ("ren", "rob", "sch")))

    def side_columns(net_id):
      return set(a[0] for points in routes[net_id] for a, b in zip(points, points[1:])
                 if abs(a[0] - b[0]) < 1e-6 and a[0] > right)

    alloc, disp = side_columns("alloc"), side_columns("disp")
    self.assertTrue(alloc and disp)
    for x in alloc:
      for y in disp:
        self.assertGreaterEqual(abs(x - y), drc.WIRE_GAP)
    self.assertEqual(runs_along_outlines(doc, routing.route_all(doc)), [])

  def test_a_second_layout_changes_nothing(self):
    doc = wired_column()
    first = doc.dumps()
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
    self.assertEqual(doc.dumps(), first)

  def test_two_loops_into_one_block_widen_the_gap_above_it(self):
    from drawlogic import drc
    doc = wired_column()
    doc.nets.append({"id": "wb", "from": {"cell": "rob", "pin": "out1"},
                     "to": [{"cell": "sch", "pin": "in2"}]})
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
    rob, sch = box_of(doc, "rob"), box_of(doc, "sch")
    self.assertAlmostEqual(sch[1] - (rob[1] + rob[3]),
                           2 * drc.WIRE_TO_CELL + drc.WIRE_GAP)

  def test_a_column_of_unwired_blocks_keeps_its_padding(self):
    doc = wired_column()
    doc.nets[:] = []
    layout.arrange(doc, default_registry())
    box = doc.containers[0]
    self.assertAlmostEqual(box_of(doc, "ren")[0] - box["x"], containers.padding(box))


@unittest.skipUnless(NODE, "node is not installed")
class TestTheEditorDrawsTheSame(unittest.TestCase):

  def test_every_mark_in_the_same_place(self):
    doc = nested()
    doc.containers[1]["title"] = "A title far too long for the box it is in"
    svg = render_svg.render(doc)
    exported = []
    for tag, attrs, text in re.findall(
        r'<(rect|path|text) (class="dl-container-[a-z]+"[^>]*?)(?: />|>([^<]*)</text>)', svg):
      get = dict(re.findall(r'([a-z-]+)="([^"]*)"', attrs))

                       text if tag == "text" else None])
    self.assertEqual(len(exported), 8)
    browser = _browser_render(doc, default_registry())["containers"]
    self.assertEqual(browser, exported)
